clue.text: Suit forever?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one of the four suits in a pack of cards
second meaning: from the Bond title and song '... Are Forever', so these gems are what lasts forever

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second sense: the James Bond film and Shirley Bassey song say diamonds are forever, so the gems are a playful example of things that last.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamonds is a card suit, and the famous Bond title makes the stones a byword for permanence.

clue.text: Professional indoor court

indicators.note: places the abbreviation inside the word just before it

parts.note: split as 'in door': the container signal, then the word that holds the abbreviation
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: It sounds like a sports professional who plays on an indoor court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indoor' must be split into 'in door', the container signal and the word that holds the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor is a qualified medical professional, the typical example of a professional person.

clue.text: Not going for Greek character in song

indicators.note: places the letter name inside the musical word

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek character in an opera chooses not to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not going' looks like staying put; in medicine 'going' is a euphemism for passing urine.
explanation.definitionFit: Anuria is the medical failure to pass urine, and 'go' is a polite word for urinating.

clue.text: Check-up before noon, first folder

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: a giro is a British payment cheque, here in the American spelling check
am stands for ante meridiem, before midday
first is written 1st, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A medical check-up booked for the morning, the first to be filed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check-up' looks like a medical appointment; in fact 'up' turns 'Check' backwards in this down entry. A giro is a state benefit cheque in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An origamist folds paper into shapes, so is literally a folder rather than a cardboard file.

clue.text: Gathering information for coach that should be here anytime now

parts.words: that should be here anytime now
parts.note: something due is expected at any moment
a diligence was a public stagecoach in France

explanation.surface: Collecting the timetable for a bus that's expected any minute.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces appear in the clue in reverse order: 'coach' comes first but its word goes second. A diligence was an old French stagecoach.
explanation.definitionFit: Due diligence is the investigation done before a deal, essentially gathering information to check the facts.

clue.text: Masterful play on Radio Three to start with

indicators.note: to play on something is to fool about with it, so the letters get reworked

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word just before this phrase is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of Three

explanation.surface: A masterly drama goes out on BBC Radio 3 to open the schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Radio Three is a BBC station, so 'play on Radio Three' reads as a broadcast drama; in fact 'play' is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and deft, which is what someone masterful at a task is.

clue.text: Preparing food and clearing up afterwards

definitions.meaning: first meaning: making up the various dishes of a meal
second meaning: the household chore of washing up plates after eating

explanation.walkthrough: The usual sense is washing up, but read literally the phrase can also mean cooking the dishes of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names washing the plates after a meal, while its literal reading fits cooking the courses.

clue.text: Quirks expose report of deceptive people

parts.note: to out someone is to expose them

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so the word is wanted for its sound

parts.note: people who deceive, said aloud, matches people who lie down

explanation.surface: Odd habits reveal what is said about dishonest people.
explanation.walkthrough: Fibbers and people lying down are spelled differently but sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Outliers are values or people that stand far from the norm, so oddities or quirks.

clue.text: No 5 prepared and cooked in the oven

indicators.note: something prepared has been made ready and reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the solution to 5 across in this puzzle

explanation.surface: Dish number five on a takeaway menu is made and baked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No 5' looks like a menu number, but 'No' is a word of the fodder and 5 stands for the answer at 5 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Tandoori food is cooked in a tandoor, a clay oven used in South Asian cooking.

clue.text: It's raw food if it's cured badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A cook warns that meat or fish which has been cured carelessly is still effectively raw.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on curing being a way to preserve and in effect cook food; spoil the cure and it stays raw.
explanation.definitionFit: Crudités are a French starter of raw vegetable sticks, usually served with a dip.

clue.text: Pay attention and join the army in the wrong order

indicators.note: the phrase says the parts of the word come out of sequence, here with its front moved to the back

parts.note: to enlist is to sign up for military service

explanation.surface: A sergeant barks at a recruit to listen up and to sign up properly.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the first two letters of ENLIST to the end and you get LISTEN; both words use exactly the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen is to pay attention to what is being said, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Half cancelling old-fashioned entry after a person one knows

indicators.note: an entry is a going in, so one word goes inside another
only half of the following word survives, the rest being cut away
the result is placed behind the little word that follows

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, then its second half is dropped
quaint means charmingly old-fashioned

explanation.surface: Someone partly scrapping an outdated diary note about a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: The first five letters of the ten in 'cancelling' are CANCE; QUAINT goes inside after its C, and A goes on the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An acquaintance is someone you know slightly, a person you have met but are not close to.

clue.text: Agreements of EU board

parts.note: French for yes, an agreement in one EU language
German for yes, another EU member's word of agreement

explanation.surface: It reads as the European Union's board signing off on agreements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agreements of EU' means two ways of saying yes in European languages: French OUI and German JA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ouija board is the lettered board used in seances, its name joining the French and German words for yes.

clue.text: Change into home gear first to get disguised

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so the word that follows is rearranged
says the next pair of pieces must be placed ahead of the rearranged letters

parts.note: at home is in
a cog is a toothed wheel, a gear
the letters of this word rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone slips into their home clothes first so they can go out unrecognised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change into home gear' reads as getting into comfortable clothes; really 'Change' rearranges 'into', and 'home' and 'gear' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Going incognito means hiding your identity, so a person incognito is disguised.

clue.text: Cause of delay, if rejected, gets the Guardian in terrible mess

indicators.note: says one piece goes inside the following word
something rejected is sent back, so the little word is read the other way round
a mess is a jumble, so the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: the little word turned round
a newspaper refers to itself as 'we', and this puzzle runs in the Guardian
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper is blamed for holding things up by landing in a dreadful mess.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian, as the paper speaking of itself, is US; tuck it into 'terrible', jumble the lot, and put reversed 'if' in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A filibusterer is a legislator who talks at great length to stall a vote, so they are a cause of delay.

clue.text: See 6
Wild 'dance to the end of love' story

indicators.note: something wild is unruly, so these letters run free into a new order

parts.note: the letters as written

indicators.note: only the last letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: the final letter of love

explanation.surface: A tale of a wild dance that lasts until love runs out, quoted like a song title.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make the phrase look like a song title, and 'the end of love' reads as a romantic finale; it just means the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short personal story told for amusement.

clue.text: Reminder for musician on vacation on irregular income

indicators.note: irregular means out of the normal pattern, so these letters are reordered
a word on vacation has been vacated, emptied of its inside, leaving just the outside

parts.note: the first and last letters of musician
the letters of this word rearranged

explanation.surface: A note to a holidaying musician about their unsteady earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the emptied musician sits over the jumbled income.
explanation.definitionFit: A mnemonic is a memory aid such as a rhyme, so a reminder.

clue.text: Not better informed on either news broadcast

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: Someone who has watched both channels' news bulletins still knows nothing more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits the news surface perfectly, which hides that it is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be none the wiser is an idiom for having learnt nothing new, still no better informed.

clue.text: Think I would dine on eggs to start with

parts.note: I'd is the short form of I would
to dine is to eat

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word just before this phrase is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of eggs

explanation.surface: Someone muses that they would have eggs for breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' in a down clue means sitting above, so the eating pieces come before the egg's initial.
explanation.definitionFit: To ideate is to form ideas, a formal word for thinking.

clue.text: Sounds like size zero is too much

indicators.note: says the answer is what the next words sound like when spoken

parts.note: a size zero garment is extra small, labelled XS

explanation.surface: A comment that the ultra-thin size zero look is going too far.
explanation.walkthrough: Clothing labels mark extra small as XS, and the two letters said aloud make the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Excess means an amount beyond what is needed, so too much.

clue.text: Legal to chase police officer capturing mafia chief involved in wrongdoing

indicators.note: what chases comes behind, so the legal word follows the officer
to capture is to hold within, so the officer's word surrounds the next piece
the chief of a word is its head, so only its first letter goes inside

parts.note: a cop is a police officer
the first letter of mafia
licit means lawful

explanation.surface: A lawful pursuit of a policeman who has caught a mob boss involved in crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legal' comes first in the clue but its piece goes last, because it chases the officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Complicit describes someone who shares in guilt for a wrong, so involved in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Some chocolate ripple? Not now!

indicators.note: some means a portion, so only part of the following words is wanted

parts.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: A child asks for some ice cream and a parent says not yet.
explanation.walkthrough: Chocolate ripple is an ice cream, which makes the parental 'Not now!' a natural reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'later' puts something off to another time, which is exactly what 'not now' means.

clue.text: Finger pointer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the forefinger, next to the thumb
second meaning: a guide that directs you to items, as at the back of a book

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one thing, a finger used to point, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The index finger is the forefinger, and an index is a list that points readers to where topics appear.

clue.text: Talk about Northern fancy

indicators.note: about means around, so the speaking word goes round the letter that follows

parts.note: to orate is to give a formal speech
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: An invitation to discuss someone's crush on a northerner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' can be a verb meaning to be attracted to, but here it is the adjective meaning elaborate.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately decorated, which is what fancy means as an adjective.

clue.text: Basic being into each other

indicators.note: other means different, so the letters take a different arrangement

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A couple keen on one another is described, a bit dismissively, as a simple thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into each other' reads as a smitten couple; 'other' alone is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Inchoate means just begun and not yet fully formed, so rudimentary or basic.

clue.text: Repeat once more, only half botched

indicators.note: something botched is spoilt, so these letters are scrambled
keeping only half of a word means cutting off the other half

parts.note: the letters of this word rearranged
taken as written, then its first half is dropped

explanation.surface: A performer is asked to go again, after the first attempt went partly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the back half of 'more' after the scrambled 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: An encore is a repeat performance demanded by the audience.

clue.text: Think again about idiots in press getting rid of extremists

indicators.note: says the fools go inside the trimmed word
the extremes of a word are its outer letters, and these are thrown out

parts.note: taken as written, then its end letters are dropped
asses are fools

explanation.surface: A newspaper reconsiders the fools in its pages once it has purged its radicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremists' sounds political, but means the extreme letters of 'press', leaving RES to hold ASSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassess is to evaluate again, so to think again about something.
